text: **Every published schema face carries `INTENT_VER` and `SCHEMA_<TYPE>_VER`, injected from code and discoverable without parsing the artefact** (D41, hv 2026-08-15). Three face types -- `SCHEMA_JSON_VER`, `SCHEMA_DDL_VER`, `SCHEMA_SDL_VER` -- across five files, matching AC-06.5's count; the three JSON Schemas share one version because they are one contract in three documents, and splitting per file would let `thread` and `issue` drift apart with nothing saying they had. **The two parts answer different questions and move at different rates**: `INTENT_VER` says which tool produced the artefact, `SCHEMA_<TYPE>_VER` says whether the contract a consumer compiles against has changed. A patch release moves the first and must not move the second. Requires: **(a)** the versions are constants in code and the generator injects them into each face in that face's own idiom -- **hand-writing a version into a generated artefact recreates the exact defect this closes**, which is the "generated artefact with a hand-kept companion" pattern this thread met three times in one day; **(b)** a surface reports both parts for every face, so a consumer deciding whether to upgrade can ASK rather than diff; and **(c)** AC-06.5's byte-identity property holds WITH the versions present, so the injected values are compared rather than exempted. **Measured before ruling (vc, 2026-08-15): zero occurrences of "version" in any of the five faces**, while the internal never-committed store had carried `SCHEMA_VERSION` and a hard refusal since that morning -- the internal artefact versioned and the external contract not, which is backwards, because the store rebuilds from the extract and a consumer's code rebuilds from nothing we hold. **Deliberately NOT extended to help text**: changing a help string breaks nobody's code. **The line is whether a consumer COMPILES against it**, which is also why the instrument is a version and not a text baseline -- a baseline tells us something changed, a version tells the consumer
